title: The Only Men Who May Have Escaped Alcatraz
lines: His head rolled onto the floor. The guard had only reached in to wake a sleeping prisoner at Alcatraz. But it wasn't a real head. And the man inside that bed was gone. June 12th, 1962.
Alcatraz sat on a rock in San Francisco Bay, surrounded by freezing water and deadly currents. They called it escape-proof.
Dozens of men had tried to break out. None officially made it. Then came Frank Morris, a quiet genius, and two bank-robbing brothers, John and Clarence Anglin.
For months, they chipped at the damp concrete around the vents under their sinks, with sharpened spoons and a homemade drill.
They worked during music hour, when the noise covered them, and hid the holes behind fake cardboard grilles.
But a hole wasn't enough. They needed to fool the guards, and to cross the bay.
So they built heads, from soap, toilet paper and concrete dust, painted to look like skin, with real hair from the prison barbershop.
Then they glued more than fifty stolen raincoats into life vests and a raft, hidden above their cells.
On the night of June 11th, they put the heads in their beds and crawled out. The fourth man, Allen West, couldn't get out of his cell in time.
The others climbed to the roof, slid down a fifty-foot pipe, scaled two fences, and around ten PM, pushed the raft into the black water, and vanished.
So did they make it? Or did the bay take them?
Searchers found a paddle, scraps of raincoat, and a sealed packet of the Anglins' family photos, floating in the bay.
The FBI concluded they most likely drowned. But no bodies were ever found. Less than a year later, Alcatraz closed for good.
Then the clues kept coming. Christmas cards arrived for the Anglin family. A photo surfaced, said to show the brothers in Brazil in 1975.

And in 2013, San Francisco police received a letter. My name is John Anglin. I escaped from Alcatraz in June 1962. Yes, we all made it that night, but barely. The FBI tested it. The results were inconclusive.

The case is still open with the US Marshals. Did they make it? Tell me what you think. And if you love people who vanished without a trace, watch the man who jumped from a plane, and the hikers on Dead Mountain, both on this channel.

structure.hook: line 0: opens cold on the shock ('His head rolled onto the floor.') in the first 2 seconds, then explains: a dummy head, the man gone, June 12, 1962
structure.5W1H: who (Frank Morris, John and Clarence Anglin, Allen West), what (escape), when (night of June 11, 1962), where (Alcatraz, San Francisco Bay), how (lines 3-9), why it matters / outcome (lines 11-15)
rehooks: line 10: did they make it, or did the bay take them?
structure.tension: lines 3-9: months of digging, heads, raft, West left behind, launch into the black water
structure.release_payoff: lines 11-14: evidence in the bay, FBI verdict, Alcatraz closes, Christmas cards, Brazil photo, 2013 letter (inconclusive)
structure.cta: line 15: question + D.B. Cooper and Dyatlov Pass Shorts with thumbnails

visual_notes: Owner asked: animation that follows the narration, page-tilt and parallax effects, real photos with motion, and NOT text everywhere (headlines only at key dates/names).
notes: Facts: FBI case closed 1979 (likely drowned); U.S. Marshals case open. 2013 letter quote condensed; FBI analysis inconclusive. Brazil photo 'said to show' (History channel 2015).
